name: inkwash
summary: Traditional Chinese ink-and-watercolour. Ink linework over real watercolour behaviour — blooms, backruns, granulation — on cream rag paper, full rendered environments.

renderer.note: THE 2026-06-09 WINNER, per bongpot creative.js:77 — Ryan: 'the style is genuinely interesting, I'm really into it'. USO dual-channel on ComfyUI on a Vast box. NOT a hosted text-to-image call.
renderer.graph: tools/_uso.mjs (buildUsoGraph) — the graph SSOT, copied from bongpot 2026-08-11
renderer.loraNote: Raised 1.0 → 1.35 on 2026-08-12 after Ryan called the faces slop. Same-seed A/B: 1.0 leaves airbrushed skin; 1.35 gives dry-brush, granulation and wash edges on skin; 1.6 is over the ceiling — scribbly pen-hatching on the face and broken eyes. Guidance 2.2 loosens the paint but costs anatomy, so it stays a per-shot --guidance knob, not a default.
renderer.aspectNote: Landscape ships (Ryan 2026-06-09) — author keyframes 16:9 so the video graph animates the composed frame instead of cropping a portrait blind.
renderer.requires: a Vast box + the :8189 tunnel — node tools/gpu-box.mjs up --rent, then node tools/gpu-box.mjs forward --port 8189

channels.identity: photoreal plate → ImageScaleToMaxDimension(512) → VAEEncode → ReferenceLatent → FluxKontextMultiReferenceLatentMethod('uxo/uno'), conditioning-side so denoise stays 1.0
channels.note: Three channels, one graph. Shots with no character subject (inserts, empty rooms) drop the identity chain and keep style + text.

styleSwatchNote: LOCKED 2026-06-09 by Ryan — committed asset, NEVER regenerate. Face-free by design: pure watercolour behaviour (blooms, backruns, granulation, cream paper) with no subject in it, which is what lets it carry medium without dragging an identity along. Style candidates are probed separately and do not overwrite this file.
identityPlateNote: An ink-wash rendered plate kept for reference. For the USO identity channel proper, plates are PHOTOREAL and scene-free (the 2026-06-09 decoupling, creative.js:41) — generate them with --plate, which uses platePrompt. The look enters at the style channel, never at genesis; that is what makes the style swappable.
prompt: Traditional Chinese ink-and-watercolour painting: confident dark ink-brush linework, loose expressive brushwork, soft bleeding colour washes, visible paper grain. Faces, hands and skin are built the same way as everything else — flat washes and visible brushstrokes, edges left unresolved where the brush lifted.
promptNote: Ended 'Nothing photographic.' until 2026-08-12 — a NEGATION, in the file that documents the negation trap, and Ryan caught its fingerprint: painted paper with a photoreal airbrushed face on top. Replaced with a positive instruction that names faces and hands specifically, because those are exactly where the model's photo prior is strongest. Content-only text is the THIRD channel and stays short. In the USO graph the medium comes from the swatch, so this string is a nudge, not the definition. On Replicate fallbacks style text is LOAD-BEARING (creative.js:161 — kontext-pro re-renders the scene and does NOT carry the plate's medium; drop the style text and you get photoreal).
platePrompt: Photographic character reference portrait, head to waist, three-quarter view facing camera, calm neutral resting expression. Plain seamless light-gray studio background, soft even diffuse light, no props, no scenery. Natural skin texture, documentary realism, not retouched.
styleOnlyPrompt: Use the reference image ONLY as a painting-technique guide: copy its medium, brushwork, ink density, colour-wash behaviour and paper grain. Do NOT copy its subject, face, people, or composition. Paint a completely new picture showing: {SCENE}. Real watercolour and ink on cold-press rag paper, painted by hand. Wet-in-wet washes that bleed and pool into each other, visible blooms and backruns where wet pigment met damp paper, granulation with pigment settling into the tooth of the sheet, hard dried edges where a wash stopped, dry-brush scumbling with the paper showing through the stroke, individual brush-hair streaks. Confident dark ink-brush linework drawn over the dry washes. Colour is muted and restrained, mixed from few pigments, never flat or evenly filled. The painting sits on the sheet with unpainted paper at the edges; brushwork trails off and does not reach the frame. Nothing photographic, nothing digital, no smooth airbrushed gradients.
styleOnlyPromptNote: For hosted-API fallbacks only. Real-media vocabulary is the lever that moved these from 'good not great' (2026-08-11): naming actual watercolour behaviour — wet-in-wet, blooms, backruns, granulation, paper tooth, dry-brush scumbling, hard dried wash edges, brush-hair streaks — pushes a model toward physical paint. The generic word 'watercolour' does not; it returns smooth digital gradients.

fallback.note: When no GPU box is up. Judge on pixels and expect a step down from USO.
fallback.alternative: replicate/black-forest-labs/flux-2-dev — 'THE PROVEN APPROACH (probe-replicate-flux2.mjs, recon_gravel — Ryan loved it)', creative.js:157

rejected.google/nano-banana-pro: DO NOT USE for this look (Ryan, 2026-08-11: 'nano banana sucks ass for the ink wash look… waste of money'). It was only ever a character-drift TEST — nano-banana-test.mjs exists to see how well it holds a character without drifting, not to render the style. Its outputs (counter.png, payphone.png) are test artefacts, not style references, and were removed from reference/ after I mistakenly rebuilt this file around them.

notes.negationTrap: NEGATION DOES NOT WORK. Naming a forbidden thing summons it — the model weights the token, not the negation. Documented in creative.js:54-59 after flux-2-dev returned a wall of calligraphy plus a red seal from a prompt ending 'no red seal stamp, no Chinese characters'. Describe the paper positively as blank and unmarked.
notes.inkWashStyleIsWrong: cutwork/config/creative.js:39 INK_WASH_STYLE says 'near-monochromatic' and 'bare cream paper dominate, generous negative space'. Live-tested 2026-08-11: that drains the colour the approved work has, and on real footage it instructs the model to DELETE the environment (a Sheen car interior came back floating on blank paper). Do not copy that string in here again.
notes.footageCaveat: For restyling REAL footage, never add negative-space or bare-paper language — keep the environment, change only the medium.

source: Rebuilt 2026-08-11 from bongpot's locked assets and the uso-inkwash recipe (creative.js:77-95), replacing an incorrect nano-banana-based version.
